title: India's plan: one trained drone entrepreneur for every village council in the country
sources: The Tribune, 2026 - National Drone Summit 2026 to Launch India's First Drone Cooperative on July 4 in New Delhi
The Financial World, 2026 - National Drone Summit 2026 Unveils Landmark Cooperative-Led Drone Ecosystem to Empower Rural India
caption:
Most Indian farmers can't afford their own drone. So the government's plan skips ownership entirely - and shares it instead.

India's '1 Panchayat - 1 Drone Udyami' national mission, launched in 2026, aims to create trained drone entrepreneurs across every agricultural panchayat in the country - 2 lakh entrepreneurs across 2 lakh panchayats over five years. Each trained 'Drone Udyami' runs a shared service centre - spraying, seed broadcasting, crop monitoring and mapping - for hundreds of farmers across a panchayat, built for India's reality of small, fragmented landholdings where a personal drone rarely makes financial sense.

Nobody needs to own the technology. They just need one trained neighbor who does.
